solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Request to admit Thunderer is too much!

indicators.note: to admit something is to let it in, so the god's name goes inside the plea

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a request to let in a noisy guest is asking too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thunderer' is not The Times newspaper's nickname here but the thunder god.
explanation.definitionFit: A glut or excess is more than is needed, a synonym of an overabundance.

clue.text: Windless California at beginning of May

parts.note: Cal is a common abbreviation for the state of California

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, taken here from May

explanation.surface: A weather report: no wind in California as May begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Still air with no breeze is the meteorological sense of a tranquil, unruffled state.

clue.text: Article about Religious Education Cardinal's produced

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the article goes around the subject's initials

parts.note: the is the definite article
RE is the school subject Religious Education

explanation.surface: An article on religious teaching written by a churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a church prince, but it is a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal numbers are the counting numbers, of which this one follows two.

clue.text: Put new top on old radio, indefatigable

indicators.note: a new top means the first letter is swapped for a different one

parts.note: wireless is the old-fashioned British word for a radio set

explanation.surface: Someone restoring an old radio set, working tirelessly at it.
explanation.walkthrough: The replacement letter is not clued; the crossings and the definition fix it.
explanation.definitionFit: Indefatigable describes someone who never wears out, a synonym of unflagging.

clue.text: Lightly cooked — that's unusual

definitions.meaning: said of steak barely seared and red inside

explanation.surface: A diner remarks that a lightly cooked steak is out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word means underdone meat and something seldom met with.

clue.text: Cite cast in play as very happy

indicators.note: letters put in play are shuffled about into a new order

explanation.surface: Name the actors in a play and they will be delighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic means overjoyed, a stronger synonym of delighted.

clue.text: Ill-mannered guy — show disapproval (right)

parts.note: to boo is to jeer in disapproval

explanation.surface: An audience is right to jeer a rude man.
explanation.definitionFit: A boorish person is uncouth, coarse in behaviour toward others.

clue.text: Talk a little covering chemical compound

indicators.note: the words cover the answer, which lies inside them across the word gaps

explanation.surface: A short talk covering some chemistry.
explanation.definitionFit: An alkali is a base soluble in water, a type of chemical compound.

clue.text: Clubs quarrel, gloat

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
a row is a noisy argument

explanation.surface: Golf or card clubs fall out, and one side gloats.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow over a rival is to boast triumphantly, an idiom for exulting.

clue.text: Step made in a frenzy? Many!

definitions.text: Step made in a frenzy? Many!

indicators.note: words in a frenzy are thrown about wildly, so their letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: One frantic footstep, multiplied by many feet, makes a rush.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden panicked rush of a herd or crowd, many frantic steps together.

clue.text: Starts to tense up, restless, nearing junction

indicators.note: the starts of the words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A nervous driver tenses up approaching a road junction.
explanation.definitionFit: A road turning is where routes meet, so a junction in British usage.

clue.text: Cruel taunt (crack) to provoke in the end a fightback

indicators.note: cruel treatment mangles the letters into a new order
the end of a word is its final letter, here of provoke

explanation.surface: A cruel jibe provokes the victim into hitting back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cruel' reads as describing the taunt but is the anagram signal on TAUNT CRACK TO plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: A counteroffensive answering an assault is a fightback in military or sporting terms.

clue.text: Odour I absorbed — dry English hazelnut chocolate

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken in, so the I sits inside

parts.note: a wine's nose is its smell or bouquet
TT means teetotal, i.e. dry

explanation.surface: A smell of a dry English chocolate.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisette is French for hazelnut and names a chocolate flavoured with it.

clue.text: Attitude (unwilling to spend) with no weaknesses

parts.note: an air is a manner or bearing
tight means stingy with money

explanation.surface: A mean person with a confident manner and no flaws.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument with no loopholes is figuratively sealed, leaving no gaps.

clue.text: Detergent, say, Conservative lists with indication of hesitation

parts.note: a ship that lists leans to one side
er is the sound of a speaker hesitating

explanation.surface: A Tory hesitantly lists detergents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lists' reads as itemises but is the nautical sense: tilts.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is one example of a cleaning agent, hence the 'say'.

clue.text: In a flap confused prince can't ski

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled into another order

explanation.surface: A royal who cannot ski is flustered on the slopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a flap is British idiom for being agitated, so frantically scared.

clue.text: Man perhaps is left without paper

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the paper's initials are dropped

parts.note: taken as written
FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A man is left with no newspaper to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Man is an island between Britain and Ireland, so an example of a small island.

clue.text: Rung of ladder dogs perhaps upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: dogs are an example of pets

explanation.surface: Pets knock over a ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: Each rung is a foothold for climbing, one stair of the ladder.

clue.text: Dad at home with metallic sound — work of art?

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
in means at home
a ting is a light ringing sound of metal

explanation.surface: Dad pottering at home makes clinking noises: is it art?
explanation.definitionFit: A picture in oils or watercolour is one example of an artwork, hence the question mark.

clue.text: After parking drink in enclosed area

indicators.note: after puts the drink behind the parking letter

parts.note: ale is beer

explanation.surface: After parking, someone has a drink in a fenced area.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale is a district within a boundary, as in 'beyond the pale'.

clue.text: Note in the morning group working together

parts.note: te is a note in tonic sol-fa
am stands for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: A memo to a working group, sent first thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A squad or crew of people cooperating on a shared task.

clue.text: Saucy, obstreperous about shows

indicators.note: about means turned round, so those letters are read backwards
the word shows some of its letters within itself

explanation.surface: A cheeky, rowdy child about to show off.
explanation.definitionFit: Saucy and cheeky are synonyms for impudent or forward.

clue.text: Ambassador with a great desire backing poet

parts.note: HE is His Excellency, an ambassador's title

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the desire is read in reverse

parts.note: a yen is a strong longing

explanation.surface: An envoy with a longing to support a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Seamus Heaney was the Irish Nobel laureate poet.

clue.text: Regular time in 1500 metres maybe

parts.note: even means steady or regular

explanation.surface: A runner keeps an even pace in the 1500 metres.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1500 metres is one race on an athletics programme, an example of a competition.
